source.title: Sparse Autoencoder Attribution Graphs Are Decided at the Margin

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It conceptually tests cross-seed convergence and representation mapping using sparse maps, feature-overlap measures, and attribution-operator transport, rather than comparing input-distance geometries across differently scaled or multimodal models.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own cross-seed SAE feature/map and operator-alignment measurements, its training-budget overlap results, and its mask-admission results. The paper does not test cross-architecture or cross-modal convergence, model capability, or whether input-distance geometries converge with model scale. Its within-model ablation and graph-prediction results do not measure the claim’s representation convergence.
record.test_reason: The study measures convergence between independently initialized SAE dictionaries trained on one fixed language model, using feature correspondence and sparse transport of attribution operators. It tests V3 and restricted aspects of V4, V6 and V7; the language model itself is not retrained across seeds.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the cross-seed findings, but only part of the paper's conclusion. Sparse maps preserve substantial operator information; target support masks discard transport concentrated on inactive atoms near the cutoff. The authors recommend comparing operators or widening target masks accordingly. More broadly, they conclude that reranking predicts intervention-induced support changes, while decoded middle-code chains failed on the one layer triple studied. They do not establish convergence across language-model scales, architectures or modalities.
record.recipe_differences: Measures SAE dictionary-feature and attribution-operator correspondence across seeds, including sparse maps, co-activity, and nearest-neighbour overlap; it does not compare distances between common inputs across independently trained model architectures or modalities, as the original Platonic Representation claim does.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured alignment varies with the matching method (one-to-one versus sparse maps), whether the target operator is masked, SAE training budget, configuration, and the input positions/margins used for mask admission. The nearest-neighbour overlap uses an absolute cosine threshold of 0.9.
record.problems: Cross-seed transport is measured on one testbed trained on pythia-70m, with no public second-seed release; the paper notes this limitation. The nearest-neighbour overlap uses a particular cosine threshold, and the detailed curve values are not stated in text. The study does not measure model capability or test model-scale, cross-architecture, or cross-modal convergence.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the within-model ablation, margin-graph prediction, and readout results in Sections 3–5 and their appendices because they measure feature-support changes or graph prediction accuracy, not cross-seed representation convergence. Also omitted ancillary fitting diagnostics and controls that do not report an alignment outcome relevant to the listed versions.

untested.parts: No convergence comparison across independently trained language models, model sizes, capabilities, architectures, objectives or datasets.
No vision-language comparison or paired image-caption representations.

Independent initializations are tested for SAEs on one fixed language model, not for separately trained language models or other architectures and tasks. Shared subspaces are not exhaustively characterized.

No task-performance preservation, activation-level substitution, layer stitching or relative-representation evaluation. Maps relate dictionaries in the same language model's residual coordinates; general interchangeability between independently trained language models is untested.
No semantic interpretation establishing recurrence of the same interpretable features or circuits across models. Geometric matching and coactivation alone do not establish this.
No similarity-threshold or neighbour-count sweep, and no out-of-distribution evaluation. The small-block experiment changes SAE training data, rather than testing OOD evaluation inputs.
No model-scale plateau test or causal comparison establishing that shared data or objectives explain alignment instead of a common model of reality.

missing.what: For the retraining pair, admitting the nearest 10% of inactive atoms recovers 0.76 of the masked-versus-unmasked gap. This main admission result is omitted from the rows.

The training-budget curves also cover downstream layer 4 and the narrower configuration's retraining pair. These trajectories are not captured by the upstream endpoint rows; exact values require reading Figure 7.
missing.versions: V3, V6, V7; shared-initialization curves do not directly test V3

record.verdict_notes: All judgments use the supplied text. Operator-energy preservation is a restricted representation-mapping outcome, not evidence of preserved downstream task performance. Same-initialization retraining results are kept separate from V3. The SAE runs share normalization and training data, and their auxiliary-loss coefficient introduces limited coupling late in training, so independent seeds should not be described as wholly independent training procedures. No result establishes semantic universality or the causal explanation proposed in V7.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of independently trained models across model scale, capability, architectures, objectives, or data; no same-input distance-geometry convergence test.
No paired image-caption data or vision-language comparison.

Tests SAE dictionaries from runs of the same Pythia model and training recipe, including independent initializations and a retraining pair. Does not test other architectures or tasks, nor whether the same individual interpretable features recur.

Tests sparse nonnegative maps between SAE dictionary vectors and their induced operators across seeds. Does not test activation-level linear maps, layer stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired-data access in other settings.
No evaluation of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE feature semantics, or circuits across models.
Shows differences among selected cross-seed alignment measures and masking choices. Does not sweep similarity settings such as neighbour count or test out-of-distribution inputs.

Reports incomplete cross-seed operator alignment. It does not establish that shared data or objectives cause the alignment, compare that explanation with a common model of reality, or test a plateau in model-scale convergence.
